items.question: How much can I compress my video?
items.answer: Compression ratio depends on the original video and quality preset. Low quality can achieve up to 85% reduction, medium quality around 65%, and high quality around 45%. Higher compression means smaller file size but may reduce quality.

items.question: Will compression affect video quality?
items.answer: Yes, compression involves a trade-off between file size and quality. Our quality presets are designed to minimize visible quality loss. High quality preset maintains excellent visual quality while still reducing file size significantly.

items.question: What's the maximum file size I can compress?
items.answer: The current limit is 500MB. Larger files may cause browser memory issues. For videos over 500MB, we recommend using desktop video editing software or server-based compression services.

items.question: How long does compression take?
items.answer: Compression time depends on video length, resolution, and quality preset. As a rough estimate: a 100MB video takes about 1-3 minutes on modern computers. Low quality is fastest, high quality is slowest.

items.question: Is my video uploaded to your servers?
items.answer: No! All processing happens entirely in your browser using FFmpeg.wasm. Your video never leaves your device, ensuring complete privacy and security.

items.question: What video formats are supported?
items.answer: We support MP4, WebM, AVI, MOV, MKV, M4V, and 3GP formats as input. The output is always MP4 format with H.264 video codec and AAC audio codec for maximum compatibility.

items.question: Can I compress multiple videos at once?
items.answer: Currently, we support single video compression to ensure stable performance and prevent browser crashes. You can compress videos one at a time.

items.question: Why is the first compression slow?
items.answer: The first time you use the compressor, it needs to download FFmpeg.wasm (about 31MB). This only happens once - subsequent compressions will be much faster as the files are cached by your browser.

items.question: Which quality preset should I choose?
items.answer: Low Quality: Best for quick sharing, social media (when size limits are strict). Medium Quality: Balanced option for most use cases. High Quality: When you need to preserve details and don't mind larger file sizes.

items.question: Can I use this on mobile devices?
items.answer: Yes, but performance will be slower on mobile devices, especially for large videos. We recommend using a desktop or laptop for best results, particularly for videos over 100MB.
